title: MEDIA RELEASE- FCCC CONCLUDES REVIEW OF ENERGY FIJI LIMITED SURCHARGE APPLICATION AND BUS FARES
text:
MEDIA RELEASE
FCCC CONCLUDES REVIEW OF ENERGY FIJI LIMITED SURCHARGE APPLICATION
AND BUS FARES
21 MAY 2025
The Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission (FCCC) wishes to advise the public and
all consumers in Fiji that it has concluded its review of applications made in relation to the
following.
(i) Review of Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) surcharge; and
(ii) Review of fares and charges for bus services.
These adjustments are in response to unprecedented volatility in global fuel prices since
March 2026 which has direct impact on the operational costs domestically.
To ensure the uninterrupted delivery of essential services, the following determinations have
been finalized.
(i) Electricity Fuel Surcharge: an interim fuel surcharge of 5.91 cents per kilowatt-
hour will be applied to the existing electricity tariff rates with effect from 26 May
2026. This means that the interim electricity tariff rate will now be 39.92 cents/
kWh for domestic customers. For example, a domestic household customer with a
bill of $68.00 (using 200kWh) will see an increase of $11.82 in their electricity bill.
This adjustment reflects the high costs of fuel-related power generation incurred
by EFL.
(ii) Bus fares: an interim fare adjustment of 22.5% per stage has been approved for
the bus transport sector effective from 26 May 2026. This means that the interim
bus fare for stage 1 will increase from $1.02 to $1.25 (increase by 23 cents). This
fare adjustment ensures operators can continue to provide bus services.
Government Relief Measures
Electricity Fuel Surcharge
Recognising the impact this adjustment will have on households and businesses across Fiji,
the Fijian Government will provide additional support measures. In addition to the recently
announced government initiative to subsidise fuel costs, the Fijian Government will subsidise
EFL’s lifeline customers that are currently under the existing subsidy to help ease the
pressure on household spending.
Bus fares
The Government will fully absorb the increase and compensate bus operators directly,
meaning passengers will continue to pay the same fares with no additional financial burden.
The Government is reaffirming its commitment to protecting the interests of the travelling

public by maintaining existing subsidy and providing additional funding to support the interim
increase in omnibus fares and charges.
FCCC Monitoring & Evaluation
To ensure transparency, accountability and accuracy of fuel surcharge, FCCC will undertake
reconciliation exercises on actual fuel cost incurred by EFL. This reconciliation exercise
allows the FCCC to:
(i) Ensure consumers are not charged for unverified or excessive fuel costs.
(ii) Maintain fairness and transparency in the tariff-setting process.
(iii) Monitor fluctuation in fuel prices and actual impact on electricity generation cost.
The above assessment will extend to the monitoring of the fuel cost impact and any further
fare adjustment reflecting the change in fuel prices will be an interim measure and will be
reviewed periodically.
FCCC is mindful of the essential role that public transport and the electricity sector play in the
daily lives of Fijians, and the impact that any changes in these services may have on the
overall cost of living and household expenses. Reliable and affordable transport and electricity
services are critical to supporting economic activity, businesses, and the wellbeing of
communities across Fiji.
FCCC continues to prioritise transparency and fairness in its decision-making process,
ensuring that our assessments reviews and regulatory decisions are based on verified
evidence, and made in the best interests of the people and economy of Fiji.
As such, FCCC maintains its prerogative to ensure that its considerations allow these essential
services to sustain its operation whilst ensuring affordable and accessible rates for Fijians.
